results.author: Gunars Mie

gpueuro #3: Verda raises prices 3 times in a week

# gpueuro #3: Verda raises prices 3 times in a week

Gunars Mie

Oct 26, 2026

Prices checked 26 Oct 2026. On-demand, per GPU-hour, ex-VAT.

Verda raised its on-demand prices 3 times in one week. Our daily checks of Verda’s EUR price page found steps on 21, 24 and 25 Oct. The H100 went from €3.82 to €4.07 (+6.5%). That makes Verda’s H100 the most expensive of the six we rank, at more than double Seeweb’s €1.89.

Source: https://verda.com/pricing 

H100 ranking, cheapest first:

- Seeweb €1.89
- Gcore €2.73 (bare metal; virtual €2.82)
- OVHcloud €2.80
- Scaleway €2.87 (approx.)
- Nebius €4.02 ($4.50)
- Verda €4.07

Verda’s other moves (19 → 26 Oct):

- H200: €4.98 → €5.31
- B200: €7.14 → €7.54
- B300: €9.05 → €9.65
- GB300: €10.40 → €11.10
- A100 80GB: €1.83 → €1.92
- L40S: €1.56 → €1.61

Nebius’s dollar prices didn’t change. Its euro prices only moved with the ECB rate (1.1193 on 23 Oct): H100 €4.00 → €4.02. Nothing else in the table changed.

...

Free compute: EuroHPC cut-offs this week. The next Large Scale cut-off (more than 50,000 GPU-hours) and the AI for Science cut-off are both on 30 Oct. Benchmark and Development access have their next cut-off on 1 Nov. If you need GPUs sooner, the AI Factories Playground is open all the time, gives free GPU access for 1–3 months, and grants access within about 2 working days. Startup credits we re-checked this week: OVHcloud’s €200 Public Cloud trial, and up to €100,000 from the OVHcloud and IONOS startup programmes. Note that IONOS may exclude Cloud GPUs.

Energy note: Scaleway’s H100 costs the same in Paris and Warsaw, but the grids are very different. In June, France’s grid averaged 30 g CO₂/kWh and Poland’s 617 g. Poland’s power was mostly coal (51%). Wholesale power in September cost €143/MWh in France and €150/MWh in Poland. Source: Ember (CC-BY-4.0). Compare countries: https://gpueuro.com/countries/

results.title: GPU rental prices are rising in 2026 — the dated evidence | GPUJournal
highlights:
### The verdict

- Nebius — Raised rates across the board. H100 SXM now $4.50/hr.
- RunPod Secure — Raised Secure Cloud rates. H200 $4.59 → $5.29/hr (▲ 15%); RTX 4090 $0.74 → $0.89/hr (▲ 20%).
- Verda — Three rises in four days — all nine rose on Oct 23 and Oct 26; seven of nine rose again on Oct 24. H100 SXM $4.34 → $4.61/hr (▲ 6.2%).
- The cheapest offers — No movement in our records. The best verified H100 offer is still $2.25/hr.

## The evidence, date by date

Every rise below was read on the provider's own published pricing page on both sides of the change — the before figure and the after figure, each with its date. That is the standard our Price Watch applies to every entry. October 1 — Nebius raises across the board: Nebius lifted its on-demand rates at the start of October, and our board carries the post-rise rates (H100 $4.50/hr, H200 $5.40/hr, B200 $8.50/hr, verified Oct 19 and re-read unchanged Oct 26). October 14 — RunPod Secure goes up: RTX 4090 rose from $0.74 to $0.89/hr (▲ 20%) and H200 from $4.59 to $5.29/hr (▲ 15%) on RunPod's Secure Cloud; both rates were re-read on RunPod's own page on Oct 24 and Oct 26 — unchanged since the rise. October 23, 24 and 26 — Verda rises three times in four days: all nine Verda GPUs rose on Oct 23 and again on Oct 26, and seven of the nine rose on Oct 24 as well (A100 40GB and L40S held that day) — the full table is below. We are not the only ones seeing it: a third-party analysis published Oct 21, 2026 found H100 prices up at six of seven specialist GPU clouds during 2026. Our own records cover October in daily detail; the direction agrees.

### Verda — three rises in four days, in full

All figures USD per GPU per hour, read on verda.com/pricing on each date shown.

| GPU | Oct 22 | Oct 23 | Oct 24 | Oct 26 | 4-day move |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $4.34 | $4.51 | $4.56 | $4.61 | ▲ 6.2% |
| H200 | $5.66 | $5.89 | $5.95 | $6.01 | ▲ 6.2% |
| B200 | $8.07 | $8.36 | $8.44 | $8.52 | ▲ 5.6% |
| B300 | $10.28 | $10.69 | $10.80 | $10.91 | ▲ 6.1% |
| GB300 | $11.82 | $12.29 | $12.42 | $12.55 | ▲ 6.2% |
| A100 80GB | $2.07 | $2.13 | $2.15 | $2.16 | ▲ 4.3% |
| A100 40GB | $1.52 | $1.56 | $1.56 | $1.58 | ▲ 3.9% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | $2.40 | $2.49 | $2.52 | $2.54 | ▲ 5.8% |
| L40S | $1.77 | $1.81 | $1.81 | $1.83 | ▲ 3.4% |

### The half that has not moved

Against those rises, the cheapest verified offers on our board did not move at all during the week of Oct 19–26:

| GPU | Best verified offer | Provider | Oct 19 → Oct 26 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $2.25/hr | TensorDock (8-GPU minimum) | — unchanged |
| H200 | $3.59/hr | RunPod Community | — unchanged |
| B200 | $5.98/hr | RunPod Community | — unchanged |
| RTX 4090 | $0.20/hr | nafnaf | — unchanged |
| A100 80GB | $1.09/hr | Thunder Compute | — unchanged |

Read the terms before you chase the floor — minimum commitments and community-cloud availability differ from list-rate clouds. But the fact stands: on Oct 26 you could still rent an H100 for roughly half the rate a rising list price asks ($2.25 vs $4.50–$4.61). Rising list prices have not pulled the floor up — yet.

...

GPUJournal reads providers' own published pricing pages and banks the figures at every check. The checks behind this page fell on Oct 19, 22, 23, 24 and 26, 2026 — there are gaps between them, so the October rises are documented check by check rather than day by day. A price change we catch in our own checks is only reported when both the before and after figures were seen on the provider's own page, each with its date; that is how the Verda and RunPod rises above were verified. The Nebius rise of Oct 1, 2026 is different: it predates our records and was an announced rise, so we did not bank both sides of it ourselves — we verified the post-rise rates on Nebius's own page (checked Oct 19, re-read unchanged Oct 26) and report it as announced. And a price a provider merely states about itself never appears on our board as a verified price. Where a provider's pages state figures we cannot verify, Price Watch reports them labelled as stated — which is how disagreements get exposed rather than hidden: on Oct 26, Spheron's pages stated the same H100 at $2.64 on some pages and $2.98 on others, and we report the disagreement rather than pick a number.

results.title: Are 200 Neoclouds About to Collapse? Our Data Says No
results.author: Chad Everett Harris
highlights:
We have spent most of this year building the SAVRN Index, and since September 11 it has checked GPU cloud prices every day. 2 Over that stretch, prices went up, not down. In fact, the sellers in trouble are not the ones charging too much. Rather, they are the ones still selling AI capacity the way a bitcoin miner sells a coin: as cheaply as possible, to whoever will take it.

...

Key figures The numbers behind this article, with sources

GPU cloud list-price index, Sep 11 to Oct 26+6.1% SAVRN Index, 117 same-item list prices 2 

GPU prices that rose vs. fell, same period 43 vs. 3 182 prices incl. spot and reserved 3 

Verda H100 on-demand, per GPU-hour$3.25 → $4.56+40% in six weeks 3 

H100 standard on-demand range$1.99–$12.29 31 offers, median $4.09 3

...

## Our prices went up, not down

The SAVRN Index tracks 229 GPU prices from 27 providers across 10 GPU types. 9 In addition, across all four markets we follow, it holds 797 prices from 55 providers. 10 For the GPU cloud market, we publish a same-item index of list prices. Because only items priced on both days count, a new product launch or an expiring discount cannot move it. 2 

Since September 11, that index has risen 6.1%. 2 

Figure 1. The same 117 published GPU prices, checked every day since September 11, rose 6.1%. Only prices checked on both days count, so launches and expiring discounts cannot move the index. Chart: SAVRN.

Looking wider, we also followed every GPU price we could from mid-September through late October, including spot, serverless and reserved prices. Of 182 such prices, 43 rose while only 3 fell. 3 

The increases were not random. In particular, short-term and flexible prices moved first: spot, serverless, capacity blocks and monthly reservations. By contrast, one-year and three-year reserved prices did not move. That pattern is what you would expect if buyers who need capacity now are bidding for it.

One seller makes the point clearly, since Verda reprices its GPUs every few days. Its H100 on-demand price rose from $3.25 an hour on September 11 to $4.56 on October 25, an increase of 40%. 3 In fact, all 23 of the Verda prices we track went up.

Figure 2. Verda's published H100 on-demand price stepped up ten times in six weeks, with no cuts. Chart: SAVRN.

Others moved too, although less sharply. For example, Runpod’s tracked prices rose a median of about 14%. AWS capacity blocks rose a median of 7.5%, while individual Nebius and Crusoe prices rose 20% and 15%. 3 Meanwhile, Azure, Google, CoreWeave and Lambda left their tracked prices unchanged.

Six weeks is a short record, and I want to be plain about that. Our list prices do not show discounts, utilization or what any provider actually collects. Still, they are enough to reject the story that GPU prices are collapsing. Outside data points the same way. For example, SemiAnalysis reported that one-year H100 rental contract prices rose almost 40%, from $1.70 an hour in October 2025 to $2.35 by March 2026. 11 

## The same H100, from $1.99 to $12.29

Here is the number that made me rethink this market. Our latest check found 31 standard on-demand prices for an NVIDIA H100. 3 The cheapest was $1.99 an hour, while the most expensive was $12.29. The median was $4.09. Our GPU page, which also counts calendar-mode and serverless rates, shows 38 on-demand prices with a typical price of $4.35. 9

...

None of this means every neocloud can simply raise prices. In fact, a price increase fails when the product is interchangeable, when delivery is unreliable or when the customer can switch to a cheaper credible option tomorrow.

It also fails when the customer’s own AI economics are weak. If an enterprise cannot make money from its workload, a higher rate just speeds up churn. For that reason, choosing customers is part of survival. Well-funded model companies, institutions with dedicated budgets and time-critical workloads can carry a premium, while speculative buyers usually cannot.

Pricing power has to be earned with things the customer values and cannot easily replace:

- Time to compute. Powered, cooled capacity on a date the provider can prove.
- Goodput. Completed training and inference work, not just GPU hours.
- Reliability. Measured uptime, failure handling and service history.
- Control. Data location, governance and auditability.
- Contract certainty. Prepayments, take-or-pay terms, escalators and remedies.

results.title: Helsinki’s newest AI unicorn on building the full stack
highlights:
Verda is sometimes described as one of the few vertically integrated AI infrastructure companies in Europe. The company operates and rents out data centre infrastructure, specialises in fine-tuning workload optimisation, and helps customers connect to, select and tailor compute through easy interfaces.

...

Over its lifetime, Verda has raised more than €390 million in debt and equity to fund its expansion. But according to Arturs Polis, the company’s early frugality has helped it scale as demand exploded.

...

📊 Hockey-stick growth. In June, Verda announced that its revenue run rate had reached $100 million, a tenfold increase over the previous 18 months. Since then, it has climbed to around $165 million, placing the company among the fastest-growing AI businesses in the Nordics. In conjunction with a $189 million funding round in September Verda reached unicorn valuation at more than 1 billion USD.

...

> “Within 20 minutes, you can add more than 100 GPUs for training your model without talking to sales.”

...

On pricing, our efficiency translates to our customers, along with ease of use. We were one of the first in the market to offer instant clusters: a multi-node, high-performance computing platform that can be procured from our cloud console, either through the API or with a few clicks. Within 20 minutes, you can add more than 100 GPUs for training your model without talking to sales or going through multiple contract stages. We’ve always prided ourselves on our on-demand compute.

# Fińska Verda wyceniana ponad miliard dolarów. Pozyskała 164,8 mln euro na rozwój chmury AI 

 Dodane: 23.09.2026 

 

 Firma dostarcza pełnoskalową infrastrukturę chmurową dedykowaną sztucznej inteligencji, opierając swoje centra danych w Finlandii na w 100% odnawialnych źródłach energii.

## Przełomowa runda serii B i nowi inwestorzy

Nowe pozyskane środki to efekt nadsubskrybowanej rundy serii B, której przewodniczył fundusz Emergence Capital. W finansowaniu wzięła udział szeroka grupa inwestorów instytucjonalnych oraz strategicznych: MUFG Innovation Partners, Supermicro, Varma Mutual Pension Insurance Company, Lifeline Ventures, 6 Degrees Capital (6DC), byFounders oraz Tesi (Finnish Industry Investment Ltd).

W rundzie uczestniczyli również inwestorzy anielscy: Ola Tørudbakken (Meta) oraz Mark Saroufim (Core Auto, GPUMODE). Wraz z najnowszym zasileniem kapitałowym łączna kwota pozyskanego przez spółkę finansowania przekroczyła 392,3 mln euro (450 mln dolarów).

...

Założona w 2020 roku przez Rubena Bryona spółka Verda zarządza pełnym stosami technologicznym infrastruktury AI. Działalność podmiotu obejmuje zarówna fizyczne centra danych i sprzęt, jak i platformę chmurową oraz badania nad sztuczną inteligencją.

Kluczowym wyróżnikiem startupu jest wykorzystanie przewag naturalnych regionu nordyckiego. Centra danych firmy zlokalizowane w Finlandii korzystają w 100% z odnawialnych źródeł energii oraz efektywnego chłodzenia naturalnego, co pozwala ograniczać ślad węglowy procesów obliczeniowych.

W listopadzie ubiegłego roku spółka przeprowadziła rebranding z nazwy DataCrunch na Verda. Nazwa odnosi się do hiszpańskiego słowa oznaczającego „prawdopodobny/prawdziwy” oraz słowa „zielony” w języku esperanto, co według przedstawicieli firmy ma odzwierciedlać wartości technologicznej integralności i zrównoważonej innowacji.

...

## Dynamiczny wzrost przychodów i globalna ekspansja

Runda finansowania nastąpiła po osiągnięciu przez Verdę w lipcu rocznego tempa przychodów (ARR) na poziomie 143,85 mln euro (165 mln dolarów). Spółka zabezpieczyła także pożyczkę w wysokości 22 mln euro od Nordic Investment Bank (NIB). Wcześniej, w kwietniu bieżącego roku, firma pozyskała niemal 102 mln euro w rundzie prowadzonej przez Lifeline Ventures, a we wrześniu ubiegłego roku zebrała 55 mln euro w serii A.

...

Pozyskany kapitał zostanie przeznaczony na przyspieszenie rozwoju produktów we wszystkich warstwach chmury AI, ze szczególnym uwzględnieniem usług inferencji oraz zwiększania mocy obliczeniowych w erze rozwiązań agentowych. Firma niedawno otworzyła biura w Londynie oraz San Francisco, a w planach ma dalszą ekspansję na rynki europejskie, amerykańskie i azjatyckie. Obecnie Verda zatrudnia około 250 osób reprezentujących ponad 40 narodowości.

results.title: How Epsilon Health accelerates radiology AI training with Verda
highlights:
Dedicated capacity. Epsilon Health needed a dedicated NVIDIA HGX™ B300 GPU cluster to scale its compute for the next generation of its models. There was no availability, it was hard to find long-term contracts at reasonable prices, and shared platforms had no capacity either.

...

Epsilon Health partnered with Verda to implement a dedicated instant cluster on Verda’s platform, with NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra (B300) GPUs, chosen specifically for what the hardware generation unlocks, not just for raw compute.

...

Fast availability, on workable terms. Verda provided capacity quickly, at a reasonable price and term length, at a point when dedicated NVIDIA HGX B300 capacity was difficult to find anywhere on the market.

results.title: Finnish AI Infrastructure Startup Verda Secures €100 Million in Series C+ Funding - EU Startups News
results.author: Lars Eriksson
highlights:
Verda, a Helsinki-based artificial intelligence infrastructure company, has raised €100 million (approximately $108 million) in a Series C+ funding round completed in April 2026. The financing marks a significant milestone for the Finnish startup as it accelerates its push into Europe’s competitive AI cloud infrastructure market.

The capital injection will primarily support two strategic objectives for Verda. The company plans to substantially scale its high-performance AI cloud infrastructure platform while simultaneously expanding its team. The startup intends to recruit 100 new employees by the end of 2026, underscoring its ambitions to strengthen its technical and commercial capabilities across product development, engineering, and go-to-market operations.
